sink: Winston console/stderr logger (utils/logger.ts toolStart->info->console transport) at INFO level on every call
guard: bypassable: pass the account password via auth.password or loginCredentials[0].password instead of the top-level password field
why: types/index.ts:35 (AuthPreconditionSchema) and :52 (LoginCredentialSchema) let the caller supply real account passwords nested under auth.password and loginCredentials[i].password; TestPageChangesInputSchema embeds both (auth: AuthPreconditionSchema.optional() at :86, loginCredentials at :74). The handler logs the raw, unredacted input object at handlers/testPageChangesHandler.ts:139 before any of the file's own redactAuth/redactEnv helpers (defined at :85-101) run -- those are only applied later, at line ~510, to a *different* log statement covering contextData/env, not to this one. Logger.sanitizeInput (utils/logger.ts:173-188) does `const sanitized = {...input}` (a shallow copy) then only rewrites top-level keys whose name contains 'password'/'token'/'key'/'secret'/'apiKey'; 'auth' and 'loginCredentials' are neither of those key names, so their nested password strings are copied by reference and get JSON.stringify'd verbatim into the console/stderr log line on every check_app_in_browser call that uses either field.
contract: "The real password for the username above. Do NOT guess or use placeholder passwords -- use credentials from the list above or ask the user."

why: create/update handlers (handlers/createEnvironmentHandler.ts:19-23, handlers/updateEnvironmentHandler.ts:42-49) log only a hand-picked, password-free metadata object rather than raw input, API responses run credentials through stripPassword()/a defensive drop before being returned, and the delete/clearSessions actions are gated by utils/confirmDestructive.ts's ensureConfirmed(); the tool otherwise just forwards uuid/name/url fields to the caller's own authenticated DebuggAI REST endpoints (services/index.ts).

get/list actions (handlers/executionsHandler.ts, handlers/searchExecutionsHandler.ts) only forward uuid/projectUuid/status/page/pageSize to a GET against the caller's own DebuggAI account; read-only, no local file/command/injection sink.

probePageHandler.ts dispatches the caller's target URLs to a remote workflow execution on the caller's own DebuggAI backend account (client.workflows.executeWorkflow); localhost tunneling is the tool's advertised feature and services/caddy/caddyProxy.ts's resolveDialAddress hardcodes the local dial to 127.0.0.1/host.docker.internal by port only, so utils/urlParser.ts treating RFC1918 ranges as 'local' cannot be used to redirect traffic to a different internal host -- no allow-list bypass beyond the tool's documented fetch-what-you're-given behavior.

projectHandler.ts/handlers behind it only translate uuid/q/name/platform/team/repo identifiers into REST calls (GET/POST api/v1/projects/...) against the caller's own authenticated DebuggAI account; no local sink is reachable from these fields.

create/update/delete just PATCH/POST/DELETE the caller's own e2e-tests resource via services/index.ts (api/v1/e2e-tests/...); delete requires ensureConfirmed(), and agentTaskDescription/relativeUrl are opaque strings stored server-side, never interpreted locally.

list/create/run/results/delete forward suite/project identifiers to the caller's own DebuggAI test-suites REST endpoints (services/index.ts); delete is gated by ensureConfirmed(); no local injection surface.

triggerCrawlHandler.ts queues a crawl workflow on the caller's own DebuggAI backend for the given URL (same tunneling model as probe_page/check_app_in_browser); its schema (types/index.ts:115-129) keeps username/password top-level only (.strict(), no nested auth/loginCredentials object), so the raw logger.toolStart('trigger_crawl', input) call at handlers/triggerCrawlHandler.ts:62 is fully covered by Logger.sanitizeInput's top-level 'password' key match -- unlike check_app_in_browser, there is no nested-field bypass here.
